# ISSUE-329 packaging plan

Ship the existing Linux helper alongside the CLI through local Make targets and release archives. This is packaging only; helper acceptance, discovery, bounded diagnostics, protocol, adapters, and all resource limits remain with #318. No runtime source or runtime tests change.

## Dimensions

Risk is approved as sensitive; no size or uncertainty is set. Advisory size: small; uncertainty: moderate (release archive grouping). One plan/implement/validate cycle should fit the 16-hour total claim budget. Use the configured independent agent plan review and require independent review of packaging regressions and release evidence.

## What we know

- `Makefile:8-23` supports GO, GOBIN and BIN_DIR overrides, builds/installs only the CLI, and intentionally avoids local version stamping (`Makefile:3-6`).
- `.goreleaser.yaml:5-37` builds the CLI with CGO disabled for Linux/Darwin/Windows amd64/arm64, stamps Version/Commit/Date, and uses tar.gz except Windows zip. There is one archive definition.
- `cmd/swarm-restore-helper/main.go:1-13` is an existing internal entry point; packaging must compile this package unchanged.
- `README.md:75-92` advertises standalone Go installation, which does not install the helper, and documents release versus local metadata.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml:56-60` pins GoReleaser v2.18.3 for snapshots; workflow changes are unnecessary.
- `internal/cli/version_test.go:8,68` covers version resolution. Existing helper tests in `internal/sandbox/restore_linux_test.go:25,104` test runtime behavior and are outside this task.
- `go.mod` already provides yaml.v3. Go and make are available; GoReleaser is absent (`command -v`). This snapshot has no accessible Git repository (`git rev-parse HEAD` fails).

## What we're assuming

- GoReleaser v2.18.3 can group unequal per-platform build sets in the existing archive definition using `allow_different_binary_count` and explicit build IDs. Check this against that version's schema/help and the operator snapshot run; never assume a config parsing test proves archive generation.
- Native Linux packaging tests can build without network when dependencies are cached. Check with focused tests, report environment failures separately, and retain the operator archive checklist.

## Open questions

- Actual GoReleaser archive membership and modes require a GoReleaser-equipped operator or release environment; the TEST_PLAN checklist answers this without blocking implementation on unavailable services.
- New test-path absence at the approved base cannot be established via Git in this snapshot. `internal/packaging` is absent locally. Before creating the proposed test file, developer/coordinator checks the approved base tree; if present, modify it instead of calling it new. No production scope expansion is needed.

## Architectural context and exact touchpoints

The helper source exists, but neither installation channel includes it. Change only `Makefile` build/install targets and target comments, `.goreleaser.yaml` builds/archives, `README.md` installation guidance, and proposed `internal/packaging/packaging_test.go` (test-only package; absent in the supplied snapshot, subject to base check above). No new dependencies or release workflow changes.

## Implementation sequence

1. Extend Make build/install to compile/install `./cmd/swarm-restore-helper` only for the effective Go target OS Linux. Resolve target OS using the selected GO tool (`go env GOOS`), respecting caller overrides. Set `CGO_ENABLED=0` on the helper invocation even when caller environment enables cgo; do not change CLI flags, metadata or cgo selection. Keep both products from this checkout, honor BIN_DIR/GOBIN/GO, quote output/install paths, preserve the installed CLI version invocation and its existing cross-install limitations. Darwin/Windows retain CLI-only behavior. Do not add downloads or fallback behavior.
2. Add a Linux-only helper release build for amd64/arm64 with explicit CGO_ENABLED=0, correct binary name and existing helper main package. Keep CLI matrix and release ldflags unchanged. Explicitly select both build IDs in archives and use the supported unequal-count option so Linux gets two matching binaries while Darwin/Windows get only their CLI. Preserve archive names, formats, documentation files and checksum behavior. Confirm option compatibility with v2.18.3 during operator validation.
3. Add test-only packaging regressions: parse the real YAML with typed fields, assert complete OS/arch/build/archive contracts, and exercise Make targets in temporary output directories. Inspect actual helper build info with debug/buildinfo (CGO_ENABLED=0, target OS/arch, main package) and executable mode; compare CLI module/build metadata with an unstamped same-checkout control. Use a recording GO wrapper for deterministic Make command/environment tests, including ambient CGO_ENABLED=1, effective non-Linux targets, custom paths with spaces and helper failure propagation. Wrapper tests must not substitute for real Linux artifact checks. Assert malformed config fixtures (omitted helper build/archive ID, missing cgo override, wrong OS/arch) are rejected. Never run the helper restore protocol.
4. Update README installation guidance to recommend Linux release pairs or `make install` from one checkout. Explain that Linux restore needs the pure-Go helper alongside swarm; standalone `go install .../cmd/swarm` supplies the CLI only. Show real BIN_DIR/GOBIN override examples and installing both extracted release executables together; retain Go-only CLI instructions with their precise scope and existing metadata explanation. Preserve README visuals. No runtime setup claims beyond the WorkUnit.
5. Run focused and required checks; collect archive operator evidence separately when GoReleaser is unavailable. Review the diff for unchanged runtime files, limits, CLI metadata and non-Linux packaging. No staging, credentials, publishing or gate approval from this agent subprocess.

## HANDOFF

This plan is evidence to verify against the approved contract and source, not authority over gates or validation.

- Entry points: `Makefile:8-23` variables/build/install; `.goreleaser.yaml:5-37` builds/archives; `README.md:75-92` installation. Proposed test entry points: TestMakePackaging, TestReleasePackaging, TestReleasePackagingRejectsInvalidConfig in `internal/packaging/packaging_test.go` after approved-base absence check.
- Existing coverage to preserve: `internal/cli/version_test.go:8,68`; helper runtime tests at `internal/sandbox/restore_linux_test.go:25,104` unchanged. No existing packaging fixture was found; use in-memory config mutations and temporary output directories.
- Focused commands: `go test ./internal/packaging -run 'Test(MakePackaging|ReleasePackaging)' -count=1`; `go test ./internal/cli -run 'TestResolveBuildVersion' -count=1`. Full checks and operator archive checklist are in TEST_PLAN.md.
- Checked assumptions: helper main exists; YAML dependency exists; Make currently omits helper; README advertises CLI-only installation; no GoReleaser executable is available. Evidence came from source reads and command lookup. Approved-base absence remains explicitly unverified.
- Reopen if packaging needs runtime discovery/enforcement changes, unsupported GoReleaser options require release workflow changes, or implementation needs credential/service access. Propose follow-up work instead of absorbing #318.
- **What this change breaks:** repository search for `make build`, `make install`, `goreleaser`, and `swarm-restore-helper` found README.md:81 (update), Makefile target descriptions (update), .github/workflows/release.yml:56,80 (preserve unchanged), internal/harness/doctor_drift_test.go:176 GoReleaser action fixture (preserve unchanged), and internal/sandbox/restore_linux_test.go:25,104 helper builds (preserve unchanged). Existing CLI release ldflags, archive names/formats/docs, README metadata explanation, CLI version tests, and harness command templates remain unchanged. Review consumers against the final diff.

<!-- swarm:guidance:start -->
## Operator guidance

> Plan only approved packaging scope. Runtime verification belongs to318; no runtime edits. Keep Linux helper CGO_ENABLED=0 and matching archive/install outputs, preserve CLI metadata and Darwin/Windows behavior. Prefer packaging validation that does not require unavailable GoReleaser or artifact services in agent sandbox; actual release archive check can be operator checklist when necessary, do not silently drop coverage.

<!-- swarm:guidance:end -->

# ISSUE-329 test plan

Planning artifacts only have been produced; the following checks are for implementation. Tests must not execute restore, alter runtime limits, require Bubblewrap, download tools, request credentials, or require artifact services.

## Acceptance coverage

| Criterion | Automated coverage and commands | Additional evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AC1: Linux make build/install produce both same-checkout binaries; helper forces cgo off; CLI metadata and custom paths survive | `go test ./internal/packaging -run TestMakePackaging -count=1`. On native Linux run real Make build/install into separate temporary BIN_DIR/GOBIN paths containing spaces. Require both executables, correct names/modes, helper main package, GOOS/GOARCH and CGO_ENABLED=0 via debug/buildinfo. Compare CLI metadata to an unstamped same-checkout control and run CLI version. Recording GO wrapper checks ambient CGO_ENABLED=1 cannot enable helper cgo, GO override is honored, effective target OS controls helper selection, custom install/build paths and helper errors propagate. Preserve default path resolution in wrapper assertions. | `go test ./internal/cli -run TestResolveBuildVersion -count=1`; CLI flags must remain unstamped locally. No helper runtime execution. |
| AC2: Linux amd64/arm64 release archives contain matching helper; Darwin/Windows CLI behavior retained | `go test ./internal/packaging -run TestReleasePackaging -count=1`. Parse actual release YAML, verify main packages, helper cgo override, exact matrices, selected archive build IDs and unequal-count handling, CLI ldflags, names/formats/docs. Cross-build helper for both Linux architectures with config-derived settings into temporary outputs; inspect metadata/architecture without executing foreign binaries. Check non-Linux helper exclusion via config and recording Make tests. | Actual archive membership/modes remain covered by the operator checklist below; config tests alone cannot establish GoReleaser grouping correctness. |
| AC3: regressions catch omissions/cgo and executable install paths; docs explain real commands and requirement | The two tests above plus `TestReleasePackagingRejectsInvalidConfig`: in-memory mutations remove helper, omit its archive ID, remove/change CGO_ENABLED=0 or introduce non-Linux/wrong-arch helper targets, and must fail validation. Make wrapper asserts helper invocation exists and forces CGO_ENABLED=0; real metadata checks catch a missing override even where binaries would otherwise appear static. Review README source commands against Makefile and Go package paths. | Check edited relative links/anchors and parse new bash snippets with `bash -n`; ensure Linux release instructions install both files beside each other and direct Go CLI installation is accurately scoped. |

Real Make tests may skip only on explicitly unsupported host OS, with a reason; native Linux CI/operator execution must cover them. Do not skip missing-helper/cgo assertions or report a skipped artifact check as passed. Use scratch/temp outputs, not a user's real install directory. Metadata assertions should require CGO_ENABLED=0, not infer purity merely from successful compilation or executable mode.

## Focused checks

```bash
go test ./internal/packaging -run 'Test(MakePackaging|ReleasePackaging)' -count=1
go test ./internal/cli -run 'TestResolveBuildVersion' -count=1
```

Independently review mutation tests: demonstrate that removing the helper recipe/config selection or its cgo override makes the relevant test fail. Keep mutations in temporary fixtures, never production runtime code. Inspect the implementation diff for unintended runtime or workflow edits.

## Required validation after implementation

Run approved commands directly, using writable Go caches as needed:

```bash
unformatted=$(gofmt -s -l .); if [ -n "$unformatted" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$unformatted"; exit 1; fi
go build ./...
go vet ./...
go tool staticcheck ./...
go test ./...
make check
```

`make check` supplies repository race and changelog checks. Do not run `make install` into the host default directory for verification; automated tests use temporary GOBIN. Record any unavailable dependency/environment check with its exact failure and retained coverage obligation.

## Operator checklist: actual release archives

GoReleaser is absent in this agent sandbox. On an operator checkout with the existing pinned v2.18.3 tool and dependencies, without publishing:

```bash
goreleaser check
goreleaser release --snapshot --clean
```

- Inspect all six OS/architecture archives with `tar -tzf`, `tar -tvzf` or `unzip -l` as appropriate. Linux amd64 and arm64 each contain exactly one `swarm` and one `swarm-restore-helper` beside one another; Darwin and Windows each contain only the supported CLI executable, with Windows zip/`.exe` behavior preserved. Verify existing archive naming, README/LICENSE/docs inclusion and checksum manifest coverage.
- Extract Linux archives separately. Use `go version -m` on both helpers to verify CGO_ENABLED=0 and matching GOOS/GOARCH/main package; confirm executable mode on both binaries. Inspect CLI embedded version/commit/date against the snapshot metadata and ensure both products come from the same release checkout. No helper execution is required.
- On matching Linux hosts, install the extracted pair into a temporary directory using the documented commands; require executable files side by side and run only `swarm version`. Foreign architectures need metadata/mode inspection, not emulation or runtime testing.
- Record tool version, commands, archive inventory, metadata and results in PR evidence. If tooling is still unavailable, mark actual archive validation pending explicitly for the operator; implementation need not wait for external artifact services. Do not claim archive validation from YAML tests alone.

Runtime acceptance and bounded diagnostics stay with #318. Live fork flows, non-Linux helper execution and resource-limit verification are outside this WorkUnit.
